items.stem: What does the 'clean core' principle encourage developers to do in ABAP Cloud?

options.text: Build extensions using released APIs and extension points so upgrades stay stable
options.rationale: Correct: clean core means using released/public APIs and stable extension points to keep the core upgrade-safe.

options.text: Modify standard SAP tables directly for speed
options.rationale: Direct core modification is exactly what clean core avoids.
Clean core is about stable extension, not abandoning version control.

options.text: Only ever write code in the classic SAP GUI editor
options.rationale: ABAP Cloud development uses ADT; clean core is unrelated to insisting on SAP GUI.

items.explanation: Correct: clean core means using released/public APIs and stable extension points to keep the core upgrade-safe.
items.domain_ref: ABAP Cloud, BTP Environment and Clean Core

items.stem: In RAP, which artifact defines the create/update/delete behaviour and validations of a business object?

options.rationale: Correct: the behaviour definition specifies the transactional behaviour, operations and validations of a RAP BO.
The CDS data definition models data; it does not define transactional behaviour by itself.
A transport request moves objects between systems; it defines no behaviour.
Package assignment organises objects; it defines no behaviour.

items.explanation: Correct: the behaviour definition specifies the transactional behaviour, operations and validations of a RAP BO.

items.stem: Select TWO statements that are TRUE about internal tables in modern ABAP.

options.text: An internal table holds multiple rows of a structured type in memory
options.rationale: Correct: internal tables store multiple rows of a line type at runtime.

options.text: Table expressions such as itab[ key = value ] can read a row directly
options.rationale: Correct: modern ABAP supports table expressions for direct row access.

options.text: An internal table can hold only one row at a time
options.rationale: That describes a work area/structure, not an internal table.

options.text: Internal tables cannot be declared inline
options.rationale: Modern ABAP supports inline declaration (e.g. DATA(itab) ...).

options.text: Internal tables are always persisted to the database automatically
options.rationale: Internal tables live in memory; persistence requires explicit database operations.

items.explanation: Correct: internal tables store multiple rows of a line type at runtime.
